title: Leveraging Transferable Knowledge Concept Graph Embedding for Cold-Start Cognitive Diagnosis
authors: Gao, W.; Wang, H.; Liu, Q.; Wang, F.; Lin, X.; Yue, L.; Zhang, Z.; Lv, R.; Wang, S.
venue: SIGIR '23: Proceedings of the 46th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
tldr: TechCD uses a knowledge concept graph with GCN embeddings and bottom-layer discarding to propagate student cognitive states across domains for zero-shot diagnosis in cold-start educational systems.
approach: Proposed TechCD, a two-stage framework combining knowledge concept graph embedding (KCGE) and domain adaptive diagnosis (DAD).
Applied multi-layer GCN over a pedagogical knowledge concept graph (KCG) to learn entity embeddings, using bottom-layer discarding to extract transferable student cognitive states.
Treated exercises as part of the KCG for joint modeling with concept entities, absorbing structural and semantic information from the graph.
Instantiated the framework with three diagnostic models: IRT, MIRT, and NeuralCD, demonstrating modularity across existing CDMs.
Evaluated on four real-world datasets (CoreMath, AdvancedMath, Junyi, ASSISTments) in domain-level zero-shot settings.
findings: TechCD consistently outperforms baselines including NLP-based and GCN-based methods on zero-shot student performance prediction across all datasets.
Discarding only the bottom-layer student embeddings (DS) achieves best performance, while discarding both student and exercise embeddings weakens results.
TechCD enables diagnostic report generation and exercise recommendation in cold-start target domains where traditional CDMs cannot operate.
Out-domain datasets from other platforms can further improve TechCD performance when accessible student records are available.
The KCG effectively bridges domains through conceptual dependency relations (similarity, prerequisite, hierarchy) connecting knowledge concepts.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: KCG example linking Math and Programming domains via shared concepts → demonstrates cross-domain bridging through knowledge concept graph.
Figure 2: TechCD architecture overview → KCGE stage learns entity embeddings, DAD stage conducts domain-adaptive diagnosis.
Table 3: Performance comparison across datasets → Tech-NeuralCD achieves best zero-shot ACC and AUC on most target domains.
Table 4: Out-domain dataset performance → ASD and LA settings show TechCD can absorb out-domain data effectively.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces the domain-level zero-shot cognitive diagnosis (DZCD) task, addressing the practical challenge of diagnosing student proficiency in new educational domains without interaction data. The TechCD framework demonstrates how knowledge concept graphs can serve as intermediaries to propagate user cognitive states across domains through transferable embeddings. The bottom-layer discarding operation provides an effective mechanism for extracting universal patterns from graph neural network representations while preserving domain-specific information. The framework's modularity allows integration with existing diagnostic models, making it adaptable to diverse application scenarios.
directly_justifies: Bottom-layer discarding extracts transferable student embeddings by aggregating upper GCN layers containing universal patterns.
Knowledge concept graphs bridge isolated domains through educational dependency relations linking knowledge concepts.
TechCD enables zero-shot diagnosis by propagating student cognitive signals from source domains to target domains via the KCG.
Out-domain datasets from other platforms can refine the KCG and improve zero-shot prediction performance.
limits: The paper focuses on educational cognitive diagnosis rather than personal finance management systems.
Requires a pre-existing knowledge concept graph connecting domains, which may not always be available.
Evaluated only on mathematical education datasets, limiting generalizability to other domains.
